chunks: So that when at last We open up the gate of severe punishment on them they will be overwhelmed with despair.

key_terms.بَابًا: A gate or door, metaphorically referring to an entry point or domain of punishment.
key_terms.مُبْلِسُونَ: Those who are in despair, having lost all hope.

ai.seo_question: What happens to disbelievers when the gate of severe punishment is opened for them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological collapse of the disbelievers as they confront the 'gate' of divine retribution, realizing that their previous denial was futile. The term 'mublisun' signifies not just despair, but the exhaustion of all hope for intercession or escape, a state emphasized by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai as the culmination of their spiritual blindness. This moment serves as a stark contrast to the believers' anticipation of mercy, underscoring the finality of divine justice.
